extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural grade-school science questions authored for standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by retrieval-based and word co-occurrence algorithms) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). It is accompanied by the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences and neural baseline models.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to collect natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests. The dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on performance of retrieval-based and word co-occurrence algorithms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests, augmented with the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: IR solver and PMI solver used to automatically partition questions into Challenge Set and Easy Set based on whether both algorithms answered incorrectly
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of natural science questions authored for standardized tests, which are difficult to obtain as most examination boards release only limited practice tests to the public. The challenge set is specifically designed to be hard for retrieval and co-occurrence methods, but may not cover all types of reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to drive progress in AI reasoning beyond surface-level cues, encouraging development of systems that can perform deeper text comprehension, reasoning, and use of commonsense knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and benchmarking question-answering systems, particularly those requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension. It includes a Challenge Set for harder QA tasks and an Easy Set for standard QA tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available via the ARC Website with a leaderboard for submitting new entries.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions) and an Easy Set (5197 questions), where the Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm (IR solver) and a word co-occurrence algorithm (PMI solver).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were collected from standardized tests (grade 3-9), filtered to non-diagram multiple-choice format, drawn from a variety of sources, and the question vocabulary was stemmed (6329 distinct words). Questions were sorted into train/dev/test partitions.

name.evidence: Together, these constitute the AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC), which requires far more powerful knowledge and reasoning than previous challenges such as SQuAD or SNLI.
